The required synthesizable top module is adaptive_aero_control_top. Do not substitute a status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module as the design top. The top must implement the selected Physical AI application contract, external model request/response transport, validation, safety, timeout, and bounded actuator-command behavior.

EXTERNAL MODEL TRANSPORT DIRECTION CONTRACT (mandatory; this takes precedence over ambiguous ingress/egress wording in upstream prose): the RTL emits model-request valid/data as outputs and receives model-request ready as an input. The RTL receives model-response valid/data as inputs and emits model-response ready as an output. Apply this rule by data flow even when application-specific ports use cmd_*, req_*, rsp_*, or response_* names. A top-level output must have a real RTL driver; never connect a required top-level output only to a child input.

FIRMWARE CONTROL-PLANE CONTRACT (mandatory): this product journey requests generated firmware. The synthesizable top must expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, transaction-valid/write-enable, and response/ready semantics. DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract must describe the implemented registers and fields. Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode; do not label inaccessible internal state as software-visible. The streaming transport may coexist with, but cannot replace, this interface.
Design an FPGA synthesizable top-level digital IP named adaptive_aero_control_top for an intelligent active-aerodynamics controller. The RTL shall not implement the NVIDIA DoMINO model itself; it shall only transport compact requests/responses to an external CPU/GPU-side surrogate service and supervise safety. The top-level shall use clk and rst_n, a compact register window (cfg_addr[7:0], cfg_wdata[31:0], cfg_rdata[31:0], cfg_we, cfg_re, cfg_ready), one bounded request stream (req_valid, req_ready, req_data[127:0]), one bounded response stream (rsp_valid, rsp_ready, rsp_data[127:0]), and compact actuator outputs (actuator_cmd[15:0], actuator_valid, actuator_fault, safe_mode). Do not expose vehicle_geometry, flow_field, surface_pressure, or any surrogate tensor arrays at top level. The register window shall support at minimum: enable, mode select, safe-position command, max/min actuator bounds, rate-limit setting, timeout threshold, stale-data threshold, sequence counters, last-seen timestamp, fault status, fault clear, and link health indicators. Implement a request packer that assembles a 128-bit request packet from configuration, flow-condition metadata, geometry-handle metadata, sequence number, and timestamp; the geometry itself shall be referenced by handle or ID only. Implement a response unpacker that decodes the 128-bit response packet into command recommendation, status flags, sequence echo, timestamp echo, and validity bits. Implement a safety supervisor FSM that authorizes actuator updates only when: global enable is set, request/response handshake is complete, response valid is high, sequence echo matches expected sequence, response age is within timeout, and no fault bits are present. Implement stale-data detection using a free-running counter or timestamp compare and assert fallback when the elapsed time exceeds the programmed threshold or when sequence gaps/replays are detected. Implement actuator clamping so the outgoing command is limited between programmed min and max bounds, and rate-limited if configured. If any invalid, missing, stale, or malformed packet is detected, assert actuator_fault, assert safe_mode, and drive the predefined safe actuator position. Safe fallback behavior shall be deterministic after reset and on watchdog expiry. The design may include small control/status registers, counters, and FSM state, but shall not use large inferred memories for payload storage. All packet fields shall be documented in the RTL comments and in a package/header if used. The design shall support synchronous handshaking, one-cycle ready/valid acceptance where possible, and registered outputs suitable for FPGA timing closure. No GPU-specific logic, no floating-point physics compute, and no direct implementation of the surrogate neural network are allowed in RTL. The design shall be fully synthesizable for FPGA prototype use and shall keep scalar-equivalent I/O below 256.
FPGA MEMORY CONTRACT (mandatory): describe bulk payload/history/FIFO storage through a technology-neutral memory wrapper that the FPGA flow can map to native block RAM; do not flatten it into registers.
NO COMMAND FALLBACK CONTRACT (mandatory; overrides conflicting generated prose): do not create a fallback command, fallback register, fallback status, fallback controller, substitute command, or fallback-on-reset behavior. On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, inhibit/deassert actuator output validity and latch the fault for software handling. Do not silently replace the requested command.
